audit.summary: One Major defect in the general reduced-space theorem: one-sided projection need not preserve symmetric penalties. A fully admissible one-element counterexample has bracket -1/210. Two Minor corrections concern BDM trace degree and an XG boundary term. The former Maxwell Minor is withdrawn: the nonsymmetric-tensor example lies outside the source Hodge/symmetry qualification and supports only a scope clarification.
limitations: P1 — The normal-containment branch of Theorem4.21 needs a projection-compatible penalty — Counterevidence: The W_tan subset M branch follows from Lemma3.13. Standard commuting scalar/graded penalties used in named examples are not refuted. Theorem3.17 is not refuted because local multisymplecticity fails.
P2 — The BDM trace degree in Proposition4.6 is one higher than printed — Counterevidence: Independently specifiable facet traces and jump membership remain valid with the corrected degrees.

proposition.claim:
Recorded check: Variations (w1,hat_t1,hat_n1)=(phi,0,c*m) and (w2,hat_t2,hat_n2)=(0,m,-m) satisfy all (19a)–(19c): volume pairing vanishes by degree, normal-vs-test pairing by zero average; flux residuals -t and+t orthogonal to M; global zero-boundary test space trivial on one element. Bracket is -c=-1/210.

K: triangle x>=0,y>=0,x+y<=1, single element. Wh: span(phi) in degree0, phi=x(1-x-y)(2x-1+y); other degrees zero. M: piecewise constant scalar traces on the three edges, both approximate trace spaces. F: 0, so base solution0 and symmetric derivative0. Edge: y=0, length1. T: x(1-x)(2x-1), zero average. M: 1 on edge and0 on other edges. C: integral t^2=1/210. Penalty: alpha(v)=v+<t,v>m+<m,v>t on edge, identity elsewhere; bounded symmetric strictly positive. Normal containment: Wh_nor={0} subset M.

Recorded check: For n=2,r=0, full P1 Lambda1(K) contains x dx, whose trace on y=0 is x dx, not in P0 Lambda1(e). Full P_(r+1) has P_(r+1) facet traces; trimmed P^-_(r+1) has P_r traces.

Recorded check: On exterior boundary, definition3.2 gives Jz_tan=z_tan, so(42b) and the preceding strong expression give check_z_nor=alpha*(z_tan-check_z_tan), not -alpha*check_z_tan. Scalar z_tan=1,check_z_tan=0,alpha=1 yields1, not0.
